```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# the code needs Windows, a running MS Word and RDCOMClient:
# it is shown, not run
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`toWrd()` writes R output into a running Word document: text, tables,
model comparisons, descriptive "Table 1"s and plots. Every call can be
placed in a bookmark and is then **updated in place** when it is run again,
so the report follows the analysis script instead of being rebuilt by hand.

This vignette walks through a short analysis of the `infert` data
(infertility after spontaneous and induced abortion, a matched
case-control study) and reports each step to Word. `tOne()` comes from
**DescToolsX**, `tMod()` from **alloy**.

```{r packages}
library(pons)
library(DescToolsX)     # tOne()
library(alloy)          # tMod()
```


## 1  Start a document

`newWrd()` starts Word with an empty document and registers it as the
current session; all later calls write there without passing `wrd`.
`getWrd()` attaches to a running Word instead.

```{r session}
wrd <- newWrd()
```

Text is inserted at the cursor. `style` takes a Word style, preferably as
built-in constant, as the style names depend on the language of Word
("Heading 1", "Überschrift 1"):

```{r text}
toWrd("Infertility after abortion\n", style = wdConst$wdStyleTitle)
toWrd("Data and methods\n", style = wdConst$wdStyleHeading1)

toWrd(c("Matched case-control study, 248 women:",
        "83 cases of infertility, 165 controls",
        "risk factors: age, parity, induced and spontaneous abortions",
        ""), bullet = TRUE)

# printed R output in a fixed font: objects are printed, for functions
# that only print (as str()) capture the output first
toWrd(summary(infert$age), font = "fix")
toWrd(capture.output(str(infert[, 1:6])), font = "fix")
```


## 2  Table 1: the study population

A `TOne` table is written with an empty first header, the levels of
categorical variables indented, the group columns right aligned and the
p-values aligned at the decimal point. The test legend follows in a
smaller font.

```{r tone}
d <- within(infert, {
  case <- factor(case, labels = c("control", "case"))
})

t1 <- tOne(d[, c("age", "parity", "education", "induced", "spontaneous")],
           groups = d$case)

toWrd("Study population\n", style = wdConst$wdStyleHeading1)
toWrd(t1, bookmark = "bmtTableOne")
```

Options: `indent` (string for the indentation of the levels, default
three non-breaking spaces), `legend = FALSE`, `align`, `font`:

```{r tone-options}
toWrd(t1, indent = "    ", legend = FALSE,
      font = list(name = "Calibri", size = 9))
```


## 3  Frequency tables and matrices

Tables are written like matrices, 1-dimensional ones as a frequency
column. `labels` relabels the row names, `digits` sets the common number
of decimals:

```{r table}
tab <- table(education = d$education, case = d$case)
toWrd(tab, labels = c("0-5yrs"  = "0–5 years",
                      "6-11yrs" = "6–11 years",
                      "12+ yrs" = "12 years or more"))

# row percentages
toWrd(prop.table(tab, 1) * 100, digits = 1, rowtitle = "Education (%)")

# 1-dimensional
toWrd(table(parity = d$parity), freqtitle = "n")
```

Any matrix, e.g. correlations, without row names or with a title for the
row name column:

```{r matrix}
cm <- cor(d[, c("age", "parity", "induced", "spontaneous")])
toWrd(cm, digits = 2, rowtitle = "Correlation")
toWrd(cm, rownames = FALSE, align = "r")
```


## 4  Models

Two logistic regression models, compared with `tMod()`: the coefficients
and, below a rule, the model statistics. `labels` applies to both,
`verbose = TRUE` adds all statistics.

```{r models}
fit1 <- glm(case ~ age + parity + induced + spontaneous,
            data = d, family = binomial)
fit2 <- update(fit1, . ~ . - age)

lbl <- c("(Intercept)" = "Intercept",
         age         = "Age (years)",
         parity      = "Parity",
         induced     = "Induced abortions",
         spontaneous = "Spontaneous abortions",
         McFadden    = "McFadden R²")

toWrd("Risk factors\n", style = wdConst$wdStyleHeading1)
toWrd(tMod(full = fit1, reduced = fit2), labels = lbl,
      rowtitle = "Coefficients", bookmark = "bmtModels")

# more statistics, other formats
toWrd(tMod(full = fit1, reduced = fit2), labels = lbl, verbose = TRUE,
      digits = 2, naForm = "")
```


## 5  Any data.frame

The table layout used above is that of the data.frame method, which can be
used directly. By default the first column is left aligned and all others
are aligned at the decimal point; the header has a rule above and below,
the table one at its end.

```{r dataframe}
or <- exp(cbind(OR = coef(fit1), suppressMessages(confint(fit1))))[-1, ]
res <- data.frame(
  Factor = lbl[rownames(or)],
  OR     = sprintf("%.2f", or[, 1]),
  CI     = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", or[, 2], or[, 3]),
  p      = format.pval(coef(summary(fit1))[-1, 4], digits = 2, eps = 0.001)
)

toWrd(res)
```

The layout options:

```{r dataframe-options}
toWrd(res,
      font    = list(name = "Arial Narrow", size = 9),
      align   = c("l", "d", "c", "d"),   # l, c, r, d (decimal), recycled
      halign  = "r",                     # header of the decimal columns
      decpos  = c(20, 15),               # decimal tab positions (points)
      spacing = c(before = 0, after = 0, line = 1),
      na      = "–",
      autofit = TRUE)
```

Before writing, `symbols` replaces character sequences by their
typographic counterparts: minus signs (but not hyphens in words),
`<=`, `>=`, `!=`, `=>`, `->`, `+/-`, `...`, ranges `1--5`, `2 x 3`, and it
keeps `p < 0.001` together with non-breaking spaces. The map can be
extended or replaced, `symbols = FALSE` switches it off:

```{r symbols}
wrdSymbolMap()

toWrd(data.frame(Test = "chi2 => p <= 0.05", Diff = "-1.2 +/- 0.3"),
      symbols = c(wrdSymbolMap(), "chi2" = "χ²"))

toWrd(res, symbols = FALSE)
```


## 6  Plots

Base graphics code is captured with `wrdPlot()` and drawn anew at the
requested size (cm), so fonts keep their size in the document. ggplot2
and lattice objects are written directly, `recordPlot()` takes the
current plot from the screen.

```{r plots}
toWrd("Figures\n", style = wdConst$wdStyleHeading1)

toWrd(wrdPlot({
  boxplot(age ~ case, data = d, col = "grey90", ylab = "Age (years)")
  abline(h = median(d$age), lty = 2)
}), width = 10, bookmark = "bmpAge")

# the current plot on the screen
plot(spontaneous ~ jitter(age), data = d)
toWrd(recordPlot(), width = 12, asp = 0.5)

# ggplot2, as vector graphics
library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(d, aes(age, fill = case)) + geom_density(alpha = 0.4)
toWrd(p, type = "emf", width = 14)
```

Picture options: `width`, `height` (default `width * asp`), `asp`,
`type` (`"png"`, `"emf"`, `"svg"`), `res` (dpi for png), `pointsize`,
`align` (`"c"`, `"l"`, `"r"`) and `newpara` (paragraph mark after the
picture).

```{r plot-options}
toWrd(wrdPlot(hist(d$age, main = "")), width = 8, height = 5,
      res = 600, pointsize = 9, align = "l", newpara = FALSE)
```


## 7  Updating the report

All outputs above with a `bookmark` can be replaced in place. Suppose the
data are corrected or the model changes: re-running the same calls
updates the tables and the figure at their positions in the document,
while the text written by hand around them is kept.

```{r update}
d$age[d$age > 44] <- 44                       # e.g. a data correction

toWrd(tOne(d[, c("age", "parity", "education", "induced", "spontaneous")],
           groups = d$case),
      bookmark = "bmtTableOne")

fit1 <- update(fit1, . ~ . + education)
toWrd(tMod(full = fit1, reduced = fit2), labels = lbl,
      rowtitle = "Coefficients", bookmark = "bmtModels")

toWrd(wrdPlot(boxplot(age ~ case, data = d, col = "grey90")),
      width = 10, bookmark = "bmpAge")
```

`bookmark = TRUE` generates a name (`bmt...` for text and tables,
`bmp...` for plots), returned invisibly. The bookmarks of the document:

```{r bookmarks}
nm <- toWrd(summary(fit1), font = "fix", bookmark = TRUE)
nm

wrdBookmarks()
wrdGoto("bmtModels")              # move the cursor there
wrdDeleteBookmark(nm)             # the bookmark, not its content
```

In RStudio the addins *To Word (with Bookmark)* and *To Word Plot (with
Bookmark)* send the selected code to Word in a generated bookmark and add
its name as comment above the code (`## BookmarkName: bmt123456789`).
Selecting this block later and running *Bookmark Update* replaces the
output in the document; *Bookmark Recreate Chunk* creates the bookmark at
the cursor first, if it is missing.


## 8  Save and close

```{r close}
wrd[["ActiveDocument"]]$SaveAs2(file.path(getwd(), "infert-report.docx"))
closeWrd()
```
